protocol: Single first request per case/version; preserve raw output and judge semantic outcomes separately from workflow assertions. No automatic retries or prompt changes to force a preferred result. Cases fixed before first generation.

cases.name: relevant
cases.expected: Accept concrete traceability, observation/inference and stale-data recommendations. Do not falsely block all advice or claim existing content is absent.

assignmentOverrides.submittedWork: I interviewed three commuting students about finding somewhere to study between classes. All described a decision between quiet, power access and proximity to their next class. One participant checks two floors before finding a free desk; another prefers a familiar location even when it is noisy. I coded the notes using access, uncertainty and comfort, then grouped repeated observations. The first theme is uncertainty: students cannot know whether a space meets their needs until they arrive. The second is time pressure between classes. The third is the trade-off between quiet space and reliable charging. I propose filters for noise and power, clear opening hours, and an indication of when availability information was last updated. This evidence supports exploring those features; it does not establish their priority across campus. Recruitment through classmates and the small sample limit generalisation. Next, I would include students with accessibility requirements and compare weekday and evening use.
assignmentOverrides.tutorFeedback: Your themes are clearly organised and your ethical handling of interview notes is appropriate. The limitations paragraph correctly acknowledges the small sample. Strengthen the connection between each requirement and the underlying interview evidence: the power-access requirement needs a specific anonymised example. Separate what participants said from what you inferred. The recommendation to display availability is promising, but explain how stale data could mislead students.

cases.name: unrelated
cases.expected: Clarify that laboratory feedback does not reliably correspond to the design report. No study-space advice inferred from laboratory passages.

cases.name: shared-terms
cases.expected: Shared words protocol and network are not evidence of a logical link. Clarify without converting laboratory instructions to software advice.

assignmentOverrides.submittedWork: The network protocol for our campus room-booking service uses authenticated HTTP requests. A client retries a timed-out request with the same idempotency key so the service cannot create duplicate bookings. The protocol specifies a five-second timeout and two retries. We tested interrupted network connections and duplicate submissions. The report explains how request identifiers support failure recovery and describes a limitation: the current client does not distinguish server overload from a disconnected network.
assignmentOverrides.tutorFeedback: Your protocol should specify the centrifuge speed and reagent volumes. Repeat each sample measurement three times and document the calibration protocol before discussing network formation in the gel.

cases.name: mixed
cases.expected: Retain supported design-research recommendations, flag the unrelated laboratory portion, and never turn it into design advice.

cases.name: two-sessions
cases.question: I have two 45-minute study sessions available to revise my campus study-space report. What should I prioritise in each, and what should I check at the end?
cases.followup: My availability has changed: I now have two 20-minute sessions. Please adapt the revision plan to the new time limit.
cases.expected: Two sessions, 45 minutes each initially; updated turn two sessions of 20 minutes. Concrete tasks and completion checks in each; no stale 45-minute budget.

cases.name: three-sessions
cases.question: Make a study plan for reviewing database normalisation in three 20-minute sessions. Include a practical task and a completion check for each session.
cases.expected: Exactly three 20-minute sessions, relevant distinct tasks and observable checks.

cases.name: infeasible
cases.question: Give me three study sessions of at least 30 minutes each, but I have only 60 minutes available in total.
cases.expected: Explain incompatible constraints and ask which can change; do not silently change count, durations or total.

cases.name: ordinary
cases.question: What is the difference between an observation and an inference when writing a research report?
cases.expected: Answer the conceptual question naturally, without forcing a timed session plan.

cases.name: unrelated-chat
cases.question: How can I better understand my tutor's feedback?
cases.expected: Clarify the feedback/work mismatch instead of translating laboratory comments into design-research guidance.
